title: Senior IT Technician
description:
ABOUT MOTORWAY

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

About the role

This is a senior, hands-on role in our IT team. You'll be the person colleagues turn to when something needs solving properly, not just logged and passed on. We run a modern, cloud-first setup, so the job stretches well beyond the helpdesk queue, covering the full employee IT lifecycle, keeping core systems reliable, and taking on meatier project work alongside day-to-day support. We are looking for someone who notices what could work better and pushes to fix it.

Key Responsibilities

- Act as a first point of contact for technical problems across the business, keeping people informed with clear, timely updates.

- Get to the root cause of issues rather than papering over them, so colleagues have the kit and know-how to do their jobs well.

- Bring your own ideas on where our IT setup could improve, and see them through from suggestion to implementation.

- Juggle the daily flow of support requests against your commitments on longer-running IT projects.

- Keep sharpening your own technical skills and stay on top of new tools and approaches.

- Act as the escalation point (3rd line) and go-to expert for the wider IT Service team.

- Coach less experienced colleagues so the team's overall expertise grows, closing knowledge gaps as you spot them.

- Spot patterns behind recurring problems early, and find ways to cut down ticket resolution times.

Requirements

- At least 4 years working in IT support or helpdesk roles, including time as an escalation point, and confident supporting both macOS and Windows in a business setting.

- Sharp troubleshooting instincts and a habit of owning a problem end-to-end rather than handing it off.

- A clear, patient communicator who can walk non-technical colleagues through an issue without leaning on jargon.

- Hands-on experience with a modern, cloud-first stack, or a genuine drive to get there, including:

- Identity and device management - SSO, MDM (Jamf, Intune), Google Workspace and similar.

- Infrastructure and tooling - networking, AV systems, cloud telephony, Zendesk and Atlassian (Jira).

- Self-sufficient day to day, but just as ready to pitch in and support the wider team.

- A real curiosity about technology and an appetite to keep learning and improving how things run.

- Networking know-how is a plus, but not a dealbreaker.

Benefits

We've got your back, in life's biggest moments and the everyday ones too.

- Competitive salary

- Equity scheme - we all share in Motorway’s success

- 25 days holiday

- Sea-front office with bi-weekly massages and free snacks

- Private medical insurance via BUPA

- Life assurance

- Pension scheme (we contribute 5%)

- Enhanced family leave (e.g. 26 weeks full pay for maternity or adoption)

- 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme

- EV leasing scheme

- Cycle to work scheme

- Nursery salary sacrifice scheme

- 1 paid volunteering day a year

description:
At Algolia, we’re proud to be a pioneer and market leader in AI Search, empowering 18,000+ businesses to deliver blazing-fast, predictive search and browse experiences at internet scale. Every week, we power over 30 billion search requests - four times more than Microsoft Bing, Yahoo, Baidu, Yandex, and DuckDuckGo combined.

In 2021, we raised $150 million in Series D funding, quadrupling our valuation to $2.25 billion. This strong foundation enables us to keep investing in our market-leading platform and serving incredible customers like Under Armour, PetSmart, Stripe, Gymshark, and Walgreens.

As the Partner Manager for DACH, you will execute Algolia's partner strategy across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with Germany as the primary focus market. You'll work with consulting partners, systems integrators, technology partners and cloud partners to embed Algolia into the multi-technology - increasingly agentic - solutions they build and sell.

This is not a solutions engineering role - you won't be architecting or implementing client solutions. But it is a solutions-focused role: you need real technical fluency, and the ability to inspire partners and customers on the art of the possible with Algolia. In practice, that means identifying and shaping three kinds of agentic solutions: those that combine Algolia with one or more of our technology partners; those built by our consulting partners and brought to market by them; and those built jointly with technology partners around a shared value proposition that delivers real value to customers and end users. Pipeline development, opportunity progression and customer wins all matter - but they all start with getting the innovation right, with Algolia at the center of it.

Reporting to the Head of Global Partnerships, and working in close collaboration with the General Manager of DACH, you will develop and execute the regional partner strategy - deciding which consulting, systems integration, technology and cloud partners to prioritize, and building the technical and commercial motions that turn those relationships into pipeline and revenue.

Algolia's partner motion in DACH is mature - we've been building relationships in the region for seven years. This role is an opportunity to build on that foundation: taking well-established partnerships to the next level, while also designing and standing up a partner-led growth strategy for the region.

YOUR ROLE WILL CONSIST OF:

• Developing and executing Algolia's partner strategy across DACH, with Germany as the primary focus market alongside Austria and Switzerland

• Building on seven years of established partner relationships in the region, while designing and executing a new partner-led growth strategy for DACH

• Building and managing a portfolio of consulting partners, systems integrators, technology partners and cloud partners (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft) across the region

• Identifying, recruiting and onboarding new partners into the Algolia Partner Program, with particular attention to partners building agentic and AI-driven solutions

• Shaping and championing agentic solutions that combine Algolia with one or more of our technology partners

• Working with consulting partners to help them build their own agentic solutions on Algolia and bring those solutions to market

• Developing joint value propositions with technology partners for agentic solutions that deliver real value to customers and end users

• Acting as a solutions-focused innovator who can inspire partners and customers on the art of the possible with Algolia

• Developing a working technical understanding of partner architectures and solutions deep enough to guide partners on where and how Algolia fits - without owning implementation

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Team

Merchant EMEA Engineering builds the technology that helps merchants join, grow, and operate successfully across our markets.

Our organization brings together the strengths of Wolt and Deliveroo and supports merchants across 37 countries. We work across the merchant journey, including onboarding, business growth and support, analytics and recommendations, menu and order management, integrations, and merchant applications.

Our teams sit close to the business. Rather than primarily building foundational platforms, we build products and features on top of our existing platforms to solve real merchant and market needs, including local business requirements, growth opportunities, and operational challenges.

📍This open role is based in our tech hubs in Helsinki or Berlin . 

 

What You'll Do

As a Fullstack Engineer, you'll contribute to products and services used across the merchant experience. You'll:

• Build and maintain production software across backend services and user-facing applications.

• Work on areas such as merchant onboarding, analytics, recommendations, menu and order management, integrations, or merchant-facing tools.

• Develop reliable APIs, data models, services, and user-facing features.

• Collaborate closely with product managers, designers, operations, and other engineers to turn business needs into practical technical solutions.

• Own features from implementation through production and ongoing maintenance.

• Contribute to technical design discussions and improve the quality, scalability, observability, and maintainability of our systems.

• Use AI-assisted development tools effectively as part of your engineering workflow, while critically evaluating their output and taking ownership of the final solution.

• Be willing to work outside your primary area of expertise when needed to solve the problem end-to-end.

 

How We Work

• Ownership: Engineers take responsibility for the features and services they work on, from development to production.

• Collaboration: We work closely across engineering, product, design, data, and operations.

• Pragmatism: We value simple and maintainable solutions that create business impact without unnecessary complexity.

• Flexibility: We care more about solving the problem than strict frontend or backend boundaries.

 

Our Tech Stack

Our backend services primarily use Go and Kotlin , while our frontend applications use technologies such as TypeScript and React .

We also work with technologies including Kafka, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, gRPC, and modern cloud infrastructure.

 

Our Humble Expectations

We're looking for engineers who have:

• An AI-first mindset, with a deep experience in leveraging modern AI tools and solid engineering principles to solve problems end-to-end, independently of any specific technology stack.

About Arbor Neuroscience 
(formerly Forest Neurotech)
Arbor is a nonprofit research organization working on one of the hardest open problems in clinical neuroscience: how to change brain circuits by design.
Millions of people with depression, chronic pain, and other brain disorders have no treatment that works. Modulating activity in the brain circuits underlying their symptoms - with electrical stimulation, focused ultrasound, or magnetic stimulation - can work spectacularly well. But it doesn't work reliably, and we can't predict who it will help.
That's what Arbor aims to fix. The starting point is a new class of experiment: intervene, measure how the circuit responds, track the symptom, and repeat in the same individual over months. We’re building the necessary experimental platform. It currently includes the Forest 1 ultrasound system, which works like a wearable functional MRI, but with higher resolution. The system images activity across large brain volumes, including deep brain structures, and will soon stimulate as well. We are also adding electrode-based interfaces in animal studies. From these data, we'll build models to make neuromodulation predictable.
Arbor is a Focused Research Organization within the Convergent Research family, and the new name for Forest Neurotech. We're a mission-focused nonprofit, doing multidisciplinary translational work that doesn't fit in a lab or on a company roadmap. We have the funding to run the first phase, and we're a small team - the people we hire now will shape what Arbor becomes.
